criteria.rule: All pages belong to the same restrained morning-lake world, without forcing a shared bitmap.
Natural atmosphere precedes dashboard or control language.
Real catch media outranks statistics whenever catch media exists.
Each viewport has one clear first visual center.
Glass protects readability and layer separation; it does not become a visual effect.
Gold remains reserved for brand, important moments, and meaningful records.
Meaningful-record annotations remain below fish, story, and memory.
No XP, levels, rarity, legendary treatment, HUD rewards, or collection-game hierarchy.
Capture button, hero-card family, icon family, type roles, and glass levels do not fork by page.

pages.evidence: Quiet full-bleed lake and brand copy are primary; the capture entry uses the shared button contract.
The recent real catch is primary; summary statistics are secondary and the capture entry follows the shared button contract.
The captured fish and confirmation task are primary; the background recedes and information panels use restrained glass.
The selected real catch and memory archive hierarchy lead; background salience is reduced and the shared DETAIL hero contract applies.
A chronological memory archive retains fish records above annotations; dense content uses a quieter background and a shared capture entry.
The species carousel stays a natural field-guide/archive experience; lit and unlit states are one FishGuideCard system without game reward language.
